stories.title: Iran issues six new conditions for reopening the Strait of Hormuz
stories.summary: Mohammad Bagher Zolghadr, secretary of Iran's Supreme National Security Council, said on Saturday that the Strait of Hormuz will stay closed until Washington "corrects its behaviour", listing six conditions in a statement carried by state broadcaster IRIB. They include an end to US threats against Iran, a permanent halt to attacks on Iran and its allies in Lebanon, Palestine, Yemen and Iraq, the lifting of the US naval blockade and withdrawal of US naval and air forces, compensation for damage from two "imposed wars", the lifting of sanctions, and the unconditional release of frozen Iranian assets. Reuters reported the June 17 memorandum of understanding had treated several of these issues as part of a reciprocal, phased process rather than preconditions. Separately, President Masoud Pezeshkian said at a news conference that "now is the best time for an agreement" with Washington.

stories.title: Netanyahu says Israel rejects Trump's 15-point Gaza plan
stories.summary: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu told a cabinet meeting on Sunday that "Israel rejects the 15-point document", referring to US President Donald Trump's Board of Peace plan for Gaza that Hamas endorsed last month. He said the Israeli army "will not carry out any withdrawal until Hamas is genuinely disarmed" and would continue to counter threats to Israeli forces and citizens. Israel has carried out near-daily deadly attacks across the Gaza Strip since agreeing to a ceasefire with Hamas last October. Last week the US-led Board of Peace said an Israeli withdrawal would only follow the completion of Hamas's disarmament, after its director Nickolay Mladenov met Netanyahu.

stories.title: Houthi drone strike sets fire at Saudi Aramco's Jizan facility
stories.summary: A fire broke out early on Sunday at a Saudi Aramco facility in the Red Sea coastal city of Jizan and was later extinguished with no casualties, the Saudi Ministry of Energy said on X. Yemen's Houthi group claimed responsibility, with military spokesman Yahya Saree saying it "succeeded in targeting the Aramco refinery in Jizan with a drone" in response to Saudi drone incursions over Saada and Hajjah provinces. Aramco chief Amin Nasser said last week that recent attacks had caused some production interruptions but no material operational or financial impact. The strike came two days after Riyadh signed a defence pact with Turkiye and Pakistan amid rising regional tensions from the US-Israel war on Iran.

stories.title: Brent crude climbs above $83 as Hormuz reopening stalls
stories.summary: Brent crude rose more than 1 percent on Monday, with October futures at $83.77 a barrel at 02:30 GMT, roughly 16 percent higher than before the US and Israeli war on Iran began. Shipping through the Strait of Hormuz, which carried about one-fifth of global oil supplies before the war, has effectively collapsed: MarineTraffic recorded between eight and 15 vessels crossing on August 4, 5 and 6, against roughly 130 transits before the conflict. The International Maritime Organization counts at least 64 violent incidents and 17 deaths involving commercial vessels in the region since the war began. Asian equities rose despite the energy volatility, with Japan's Nikkei 225 up 2.1 percent, South Korea's Kospi up 0.7 percent and Hong Kong's Hang Seng up 0.6 percent.

stories.title: 60,000-year-old ostrich eggshell engravings show rule-based geometric thinking
stories.summary: A study led by the University of Bologna analysed 112 engraved ostrich eggshell fragments from Diepkloof and Klipdrift in South Africa and Apollo 11 in Namibia, dating to more than 60,000 years ago. More than 80 percent of the configurations contained consistent spatial patterns, including repeated near-90-degree angles, sets of parallel lines, hatched bands, grids and diamond motifs showing rotation, translation, repetition and hierarchical embedding. The authors argue the designs followed deliberate geometric rules rather than being improvised, indicating visuo-spatial planning before carving. The paper, "Earliest geometries: A cognitive investigation of Howiesons Poort engraved ostrich eggshells", was published in PLOS One.

stories.title: Trial finds three daily servings of full-fat dairy did not worsen weight or cholesterol
stories.summary: A 12-week randomised study of 74 adults with overweight or obesity, led by University of Toronto professor Harvey Anderson, found no meaningful differences in weight gain, body composition or cholesterol between a low-dairy calorie-restricted diet and diets including three daily servings of full-fat dairy. Participants in the dairy groups showed improvements in blood pressure and consumed more calcium, protein and vitamin D, with no evidence of insulin resistance. The authors point to the "dairy matrix hypothesis", the idea that the physical structure of dairy foods affects how their nutrients are digested and absorbed, as a possible explanation. The findings were published in The Journal of Nutrition.
